pytensor 3.0.7


One container holds everything an algorithm may ever need from an environment. The transition tensor \(P[s,a,s']\) and the reward mean/sd tables \(r_\mu[s,a], r_\sigma[s,a]\) are used in exactly two places:

The simulator samples \(S_{t+1}\sim P[s,a,\cdot]\) and \(R_{t+1}\sim\mathcal N(r_\mu, r_\sigma)\)
DP oracle sweeps them to compute exact values to serve as the answer key.

The learning algorithms don’t have access to either.
Two extra parameters are needed for environments of this chapter:

legal_actions marks which actions are legal in each state (the maximization-bias MDP has 2 actions in one state and 10 in another)
reachable marks the states that can actually be occupied (cliff walking has cells you can fall into but never stand on).


NEG_INF = -1e30   # stand-in for -inf when masking illegal actions

@dataclass
class Env:
    name: str
    n_states: int
    n_actions: int
    P: np.ndarray              # (n_states, n_actions, n_states) transition probabilities
    reward_mean: np.ndarray    # (n_states, n_actions)
    reward_sd: np.ndarray      # (n_states, n_actions)
    terminal: np.ndarray       # (n_states,) bool
    start: np.ndarray          # (n_states,) start-state distribution
    legal_actions: np.ndarray  # (n_states, n_actions) 1.0 where the action is allowed
    reachable: np.ndarray      # (n_states,) reachable from a start state
    shape: tuple = ()          # grid shape, for printing


def make_env(name, n_states, n_actions, step_fn, terminals, starts, shape=(), legal_actions=None):
    "step_fn(s, a) returns (s_next, reward_mean, reward_sd); terminals absorb with reward 0."
    P = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions, n_states))
    reward_mean = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    reward_sd = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    terminal = np.zeros(n_states, dtype=bool); terminal[list(terminals)] = True

    for s in range(n_states):
        for a in range(n_actions):
            if terminal[s]:
                P[s, a, s] = 1.0
                continue
            s_next, mean, sd = step_fn(s, a)
            P[s, a, s_next] = 1.0
            reward_mean[s, a] = mean
            reward_sd[s, a] = sd

    start = np.zeros(n_states)
    start[list(starts)] = 1.0 / len(list(starts))

    if legal_actions is None:
        legal_actions = np.ones((n_states, n_actions))

    reachable = start > 0 # Breadth-First-Search over the legal actions
    legal_P = P * (legal_actions > 0)[:, :, None] # illegal (s, a) rows zeroed out
    while True:
        frontier = legal_P[reachable & ~terminal] # transitions out of reachable, non-terminal states
        one_step_reachable = frontier.sum(axis=(0, 1)) > 0
        grown = reachable | one_step_reachable
        if grown.sum() == reachable.sum(): # No new states are reachable
            break
        reachable = grown

    return Env(
        name,
        n_states,
        n_actions,
        P,
        reward_mean,
        reward_sd,
        terminal,
        start,
        legal_actions,
        reachable,
        shape
    )


UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT = 0, 1, 2, 3
ARROWS = {UP: "^", DOWN: "v", LEFT: "<", RIGHT: ">"}

def _move(row, col, action, n_rows, n_cols):
    if action == UP: row = max(row - 1, 0)
    elif action == DOWN: row = min(row + 1, n_rows - 1)
    elif action == LEFT: col = max(col - 1, 0)
    elif action == RIGHT: col = min(col + 1, n_cols - 1)
    return row, col

def show_grid(values, env, title="", fmt="6.1f"):
    if title: print(title)
    n_rows, n_cols = env.shape
    for row in np.asarray(values, dtype=float).reshape(n_rows, n_cols):
        print("  " + "  ".join(f"{x:{fmt}}" for x in row))

def show_policy(actions, env, title="", extra=None):
    "extra: dict cell -> character, drawn on top (terminals, cliff, start, ...)"
    if title: print(title)
    n_rows, n_cols = env.shape
    chars = [ARROWS[int(a)] for a in actions]
    for s in np.flatnonzero(env.terminal): chars[s] = "T"
    for s in np.flatnonzero(~env.reachable): chars[s] = "."
    for s, ch in (extra or {}).items(): chars[s] = ch
    for row in range(n_rows):
        print("   " + " ".join(chars[row * n_cols:(row + 1) * n_cols]))

The five environments are all undiscounted (\(\gamma = 1\)) with \(-1\) reward per step unless noted.








Env
Shape
What it is




grid4
\(4\times4\)
Terminal corners 0 and 15, episodes start uniformly on a non-terminal cell. Our workbench for prediction, because we know \(v_\pi\) and \(v_*\) exactly.


walk5
\(1\times5\)
Five states in a row, absorbing ends, reward \(+1\) only on stepping off the right end, always starting in the centre. Under the random policy \(v_\pi(i) = i/6\) - values small enough that TD and MC can be compared cleanly.


cliff
\(4\times12\)
Stepping into the bottom-row cliff costs \(-100\) and teleports you back to the start (the episode does not end).


windy
\(7\times10\)
An upward wind displaces you by 0-2 cells depending on the column you leave from.


maxbias
2 decision states
From A you may go left into B or right to terminate; every one of B’s ten actions terminates with reward \(\mathcal N(-0.1, 1)\). Going left is always a mistake in expectation, which is what makes it a trap for a learner that maximizes over noisy estimates.




# Remember our environment factory takes:
# name, n_states, n_actions, step_fn, terminals, starts, shape=(), legal_actions=None
# as arguments

def grid4_env():
    def step(s, a):
        "return next_state, reward_mean, reward_sd"
        row, col = _move(*divmod(s, 4), a, 4, 4)
        return row * 4 + col, -1.0, 0.0
    return make_env("grid4", 16, 4, step, [0, 15],
                    [s for s in range(16) if s not in (0, 15)], shape=(4, 4))

def walk5_env():
    def step(s, a): # a = 0 left, a = 1 right
        s_next = s - 1 if a == 0 else s + 1
        return s_next, 1.0 if s_next == 6 else 0.0, 0.0
    return make_env("walk5", 7, 2, step, [0, 6], [3], shape=(1, 7))

def cliff_env(n_rows=4, n_cols=12):
    start_state = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols
    goal = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols + n_cols - 1
    cliff_cells = {(n_rows - 1) * n_cols + col for col in range(1, n_cols - 1)}
    def step(s, a):
        row, col = _move(*divmod(s, n_cols), a, n_rows, n_cols)
        s_next = row * n_cols + col
        return (start_state, -100.0, 0.0) if s_next in cliff_cells else (s_next, -1.0, 0.0)
    return make_env("cliff", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [goal], [start_state],
                    shape=(n_rows, n_cols))

WIND = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0])

def windy_env(n_rows=7, n_cols=10):
    def step(s, a):
        row, col = divmod(s, n_cols)
        row_next, col_next = _move(row, col, a, n_rows, n_cols)
        row_next = max(row_next - WIND[col], 0)   # wind of the column you leave, blowing up
        return row_next * n_cols + col_next, -1.0, 0.0
    return make_env("windy", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [3 * n_cols + 7], [3 * n_cols],
                    shape=(n_rows, n_cols))

def maxbias_env(n_B_actions=10, mean=-0.1, sd=1.0):
    # 0 = A (start), 1 = B, 2 = terminal. A: 0 = left -> B, 1 = right -> terminal
    legal_actions = np.zeros((3, n_B_actions))
    legal_actions[0, :2] = 1.0 # only left(0) and right(1) are legal
    legal_actions[1:, :] = 1.0 # B: all n_B_actions and terminal are legal
    def step(s, a):
        if s == 0:
            return (1, 0.0, 0.0) if a == 0 else (2, 0.0, 0.0)
        return 2, mean, sd
    return make_env("maxbias", 3, n_B_actions, step, [2], [0], legal_actions=legal_actions)

grid4, walk5, cliff, windy, maxbias = (grid4_env(), walk5_env(), cliff_env(), windy_env(), maxbias_env())

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
DP Oracle
We perform two sweeps per environment using our DP oracle. First, iterative policy evaluation for \(v_\pi\), and second, value iteration for \(v_*\). In addition, we compute the one-step lookahead \[
q(s,a) = r(s,a) + \gamma\sum_{s'}P[s,a,s']\,v(s')
\]
that turns any state-value vector into action values. Illegal actions are masked out of the \(\max\) with a large negative number.

def make_dp(env, n_iters=2000):
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    gamma = pt.scalar("gamma")
    pi = pt.matrix("pi")
    v_in = pt.vector("v")

    def q_from(v, gamma):
        return reward + gamma * (P * v[None, None, :]).sum(axis=2)

    def expectation_step(v, pi, gamma): # v_{k+1}(s) = sum_a pi(a|s) q_k(s, a)
        return not_terminal * (pi * q_from(v, gamma)).sum(axis=1)

    def optimality_step(v, gamma): # v_{k+1}(s) = max over the legal a of q_k(s, a)
        q = pt.where(legal_actions > 0, q_from(v, gamma), NEG_INF)
        return not_terminal * q.max(axis=1)

    v_eval = pytensor.scan(
        fn=expectation_step,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((env.n_states,)),
        non_sequences=[pi, gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )

    v_star = pytensor.scan(
        fn=optimality_step,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((env.n_states,)),
        non_sequences=[gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )
    return (pytensor.function([pi, gamma], v_eval[-1]), # evaluate_policy
            pytensor.function([gamma], v_star[-1]), # optimal_values
            pytensor.function([v_in, gamma], q_from(v_in, gamma))) # action_values_of


ORACLE = {e.name: make_dp(e) for e in (grid4, walk5, cliff, windy, maxbias)}

def exact(env, gamma=1.0, pi=None):
    "v_pi if a policy is given, else v_*; always with the matching action values."
    evaluate_policy, optimal_values, action_values_of = ORACLE[env.name]
    v = evaluate_policy(pi, gamma) if pi is not None else optimal_values(gamma)
    q = action_values_of(v, gamma)
    q[env.terminal] = 0.0
    return v, q

pi_random_g4 = np.ones((grid4.n_states, grid4.n_actions)) / grid4.n_actions
v_pi_g4, q_pi_g4 = exact(grid4, 1.0, pi_random_g4)
v_star_g4, q_star_g4 = exact(grid4)

show_grid(v_pi_g4, grid4, "exact v_pi, equiprobable random policy:")
print()
show_grid(v_star_g4, grid4, "exact v_* :")

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Simulator
For prediction (policy evaluation) we need episodes generated by a fixed policy, so we reuse the batched rollout of the Monte Carlo chapter where the recurrent state of the scan is a length-\(B\) vector of current states, and every step draws
\[
A_t\sim\pi(\cdot\mid S_t)
\]
\[
S_{t+1}\sim P[S_t,A_t,\cdot]
\]
\[
R_{t+1}\sim\mathcal N(r_\mu, r_\sigma)
\]
for all \(B\) episodes at once.
The RNG is threaded through scan as one of the recurrent outputs and registered in updates= so successive calls continue the stream. Terminal states absorb with reward 0, so the padded steps after termination contribute nothing and are masked out of every statistic.
The rollout returns aligned \((T,B)\) tensors, each row \(t\) holding \((S_t, A_t, R_{t+1}, S_{t+1})\), where the TD update needs that fourth element compared to Monte Carlo.

def make_rollout(env, seed):
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward_mean = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    reward_sd = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_sd)
    rng_shared = pt.random.shared_rng(seed=seed, name=f"rng_roll_{env.name}")
    pi = pt.matrix("pi")
    s_start = pt.lvector("s0")
    max_steps = pt.iscalar("T")

    def step(s, rng, pi):
        rng, a = rng.categorical(p=pi[s]) # A_t ~ pi(.|S_t)
        rng, s_next = rng.categorical(p=P[s, a]) # S_{t+1} ~ p(.|S_t,A_t)
        rng, r = rng.normal(loc=reward_mean[s, a], scale=reward_sd[s, a]) # R_{t+1}
        return s_next, rng, a, r

    S_next, rng_final, A, R = pytensor.scan(
        fn=step,
        outputs_info=[s_start, rng_shared, None, None],
        non_sequences=[pi],
        n_steps=max_steps,
        return_updates=False
    )
    S = pt.concatenate([s_start[None, :], S_next[:-1]], axis=0) # row t = S_t
    return pytensor.function([pi, s_start, max_steps], [S, A, R, S_next], updates={rng_shared: rng_final})

def make_returns():
    "G_t = R_{t+1} + gamma * G_{t+1}, backward updates."
    R = pt.matrix("R")
    gamma = pt.scalar("g")

    def accumulate_return(r, G_next, gamma):
        return r + gamma * G_next # R_{t+1} + gamma * G_{t+1}

    G = pytensor.scan(
        fn=accumulate_return,
        sequences=[R],
        outputs_info=pt.zeros_like(R[0]),
        non_sequences=[gamma],
        go_backwards=True, return_updates=False
    )
    return pytensor.function([R, gamma], G[::-1])

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Sequential updates as a scan
TD is strictly sequential, each update uses the \(V\) produced by the previous update. So the scan carries \(V\) as its recurrent state and walks the transitions in order.
We define two scans:

the inner one steps through the transitions of one episode
the outer one steps through episodes and hands back \(V\) after each, yielding a learning curve

In the previous chapter MC ran thousands of episodes in parallel along a batch dimension, because averaging returns is order-independent. Online TD cannot do that because episode \(k+1\) must see the \(V\) that episode \(k\) produced. What we can still parallelize is independent runs of separate learners with their own \(V\) (and their own \(\alpha\), which is how we sweep step sizes). So \(V\) has shape (n_runs, n_states) and every update is a batched inc_subtensor.

def make_predict(env, kind):
    """TD(0) (kind='td0') or constant-alpha every-visit MC (kind='mc') prediction.
    Episodes come in as (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners); returns V after each episode."""
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    S_all = pt.ltensor3("S")
    targets_all = pt.dtensor3("X")
    S_next_all = pt.ltensor3("Sp")
    V_init = pt.dmatrix("V0")
    alpha = pt.dvector("alpha")
    gamma = pt.scalar("g")

    def transition(s, x, s_next, V, alpha, gamma):
        learners = pt.arange(V.shape[0])
        still_running = not_terminal[s] # skip padding after termination
        # x is R_{t+1} for TD(0) (bootstrap off V(S_{t+1})), and G_t for MC
        target = (x + gamma * not_terminal[s_next] * V[learners, s_next]
                  if kind == "td0" else x)
        return pt.inc_subtensor(V[learners, s],
                                alpha * still_running * (target - V[learners, s]))

    def episode(S_ep, targets_ep, S_next_ep, V, alpha, gamma):
        V_steps = pytensor.scan(fn=transition, sequences=[S_ep, targets_ep, S_next_ep],
                                outputs_info=V, non_sequences=[alpha, gamma],
                                return_updates=False)
        return V_steps[-1]

    V_per_episode = pytensor.scan(fn=episode, sequences=[S_all, targets_all, S_next_all],
                                  outputs_info=V_init, non_sequences=[alpha, gamma],
                                  return_updates=False)
    return pytensor.function([S_all, targets_all, S_next_all, V_init, alpha, gamma],
                             V_per_episode)

td0_g4 = make_predict(grid4, "td0")
mc_g4 = make_predict(grid4, "mc")


def episodes_for(rollout, env, pi, n_episodes, n_learners, max_steps, gamma=1.0):
    """One rollout call, reshaped into (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners) so that learner r
    sees its own stream of n_episodes episodes in order."""
    n_chains = n_episodes * n_learners
    s_start = np_rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(env.start > 0), size=n_chains,
                            p=env.start[env.start > 0]).astype("int64")
    S, A, R, S_next = rollout(pi, s_start, max_steps)
    G = returns_fn(R, gamma)
    by_episode = lambda X: X.reshape(max_steps, n_episodes, n_learners).transpose(1, 0, 2)
    frac_finished = env.terminal[S_next[-1]].mean()
    return (by_episode(S), by_episode(A), by_episode(R), by_episode(S_next),
            by_episode(G), frac_finished)

def rmse_over_states(V, v_true, states):
    "V: (n_episodes, n_learners, n_states) -> (n_episodes, n_learners) RMSE over `states`."
    return np.sqrt(((V[:, :, states] - v_true[states]) ** 2).mean(axis=2))

Every curve plateaus rather than converging to zero. With a fixed \(\alpha\) the estimate keeps chasing the most recent samples, so it settles into a noise band around \(v_\pi\) whose width grows with \(\alpha\).
Monte Carlo descends first, but TD ends up more accurate. This is the bias-variance off, where MC’s target is an unbiased sample of the right magnitude, so from the cold start \(V=0\) it lands in the right ballpark almost immediately. Whereas, TD which bootstraps off its own wrong values, has to diffuse the terminal-state information outward roughly one state per visit. However, when TD’s estimates are in the right ballpark the situation reverses because returns on this gridworld are wildly variable (the random policy’s episode lengths range from a couple of steps to dozens), MC keeps jumping toward noisy targets and never settles, but TD’s target is anchored by an estimate that is already nearly right.
Larger \(\alpha\) is faster early and worse late - and it hurts MC much more than TD, for the same reason.

TD learning faster is not unconditional. MC pays for varianc while TD pays for bias, however, the bias is transient as TD will eventually convegerge on the correct estimate, but the variance is not as MC will continue jumping toward noisy targets.

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Driving Home Problem
You leave the office and predict how long the drive home will take, revising the prediction as things unfold. Each leg’s elapsed time is a reward and the prediction is the value: total time = elapsed so far + predicted time to go.
An MC learner can only update once it is home (end of the episode), and then it shifts every prediction of the trip toward the single outcome. A TD learner shifts each prediction toward the next prediction, as soon as that next prediction exists. For example, when you reach the car in the rain and revise 30 minutes to 40 minutes, the TD learner immediately corrects the “leaving office” estimate, without waiting to see whether the rest of the drive was lucky.

V_drive_td[:-1] = leg_cost + V_drive[1:] # alpha = 1: target R + V(next)

The table above is hard-coded and covers a single trip, which makes it a diagram rather than an experiment. We cannot see a rate in just one episode.
So here is the same commute as an actual environment, driven 1000 times.
Randomness is carried by the action draw where the rollout samples \(A_t\sim\pi(\cdot\mid S_t)\) and then continues on deterministically, so a fixed \(\pi\) collapses this MDP into the Markov chain, and we reuse make_env, the rollout, make_predict, and the DP oracle that supplies the answer key.
Two branching scenarios make the trip stochastic:

it rains with probability \(0.3\) (costing 5 minutes on the highway leg)
you get stuck behind a slow truck with probability \(0.4\) (costing 6 minutes).

Each leg’s duration is itself noisy, so no two commutes are alike.
Both learners are initialised with the static example’s own table, \([30, 30, 35, 15, 10, 3, 0]\).

OFFICE, CAR_DRY, CAR_RAIN, EXIT_HWY, TRUCK, STREET, HOME = range(7)

DRIVE_STATES = ["leaving office", "at car, dry", "at car, raining",
                "exiting highway", "behind truck", "home street", "home"]

P_RAIN, P_TRUCK = 0.3, 0.4

DRIVE_LEGS = { # (state, scenario/branch) -> (next state, mean minutes, sd)
    (OFFICE, 0): (CAR_DRY, 5.0, 1.0),
    (OFFICE, 1): (CAR_RAIN, 5.0, 1.0),
    (CAR_DRY, 0): (EXIT_HWY, 13.0, 2.0),
    (CAR_RAIN, 0): (EXIT_HWY, 18.0, 3.0), # rain costs 5 minutes on the highway leg
    (EXIT_HWY, 0): (STREET, 12.0, 1.5),
    (EXIT_HWY, 1): (TRUCK, 10.0, 1.0),
    (TRUCK, 0): (STREET, 8.0, 1.5), # the truck detour: 10 + 8 instead of 12
    (STREET, 0): (HOME, 3.0, 0.5),
}

def drive_env():
    def step(s, a):
        return DRIVE_LEGS.get((s, a), DRIVE_LEGS[(s, 0)]) # branch 1 == branch 0 where unbranched
    return make_env("drive", 7, 2, step, [HOME], [OFFICE], shape=(1, 7))

TD’s target is one 5-minute walk to the car plus a stored estimate of the rest, so it barely moves.

MC’s target accumulates noise from every remaining leg, while TD’s always sees exactly one. So lengthening the trip should hurt MC but not TD.

# stretch the commute by inserting extra highway legs.
def make_long_drive(n_highway, name):
    hwy0 = 3
    truck = hwy0 + n_highway
    street = truck + 1
    home = street + 1

    legs = {
        (OFFICE, 0): (CAR_DRY, 5.0, 1.0),
        (OFFICE, 1): (CAR_RAIN, 5.0, 1.0),
        (CAR_DRY, 0): (hwy0, 13.0, 2.0),
        (CAR_RAIN, 0): (hwy0, 18.0, 3.0),
        (truck, 0): (street, 8.0, 1.5),
        (street, 0): (home, 3.0, 0.5)
    }

    for i in range(n_highway - 1):
        legs[(hwy0 + i, 0)] = (hwy0 + i + 1, 4.0, 1.5)

    legs[(hwy0 + n_highway - 1, 0)] = (street, 12.0, 1.5)
    legs[(hwy0 + n_highway - 1, 1)] = (truck, 10.0, 1.0)

    env = make_env(name, home + 1, 2, lambda s, a: legs.get((s, a), legs[(s, 0)]), [home], [OFFICE])

    pi = np.zeros((env.n_states, 2))
    pi[:, 0] = 1.0
    pi[OFFICE] = [1 - P_RAIN, P_RAIN]
    pi[hwy0 + n_highway - 1] = [1 - P_TRUCK, P_TRUCK]
    return env, pi

print("alpha = 0.05, 1000 trips, both started from the exact values plus N(0, 3) noise")
print(f"{'legs':>5} {'return sd':>10} {'TD(0)':>8} {'MC':>8} {'MC/TD':>7}")
for n_highway in (1, 3, 6, 12):
    env_l, pi_l = make_long_drive(n_highway, f"drive_long{n_highway}")
    ORACLE[env_l.name] = make_dp(env_l)
    v_true_l, _ = exact(env_l, 1.0, pi_l)
    S_l, _, R_l, S_next_l, G_l, _ = episodes_for(make_rollout(env_l, 99), env_l, pi_l,
                                                 N_EPISODES_D, N_RUNS_D, n_highway + 7)
    V0_l = v_true_l + np_rng.normal(size=(N_RUNS_D, env_l.n_states)) * 3.0
    V0_l[:, env_l.terminal] = 0.0
    alpha_l = np.full(N_RUNS_D, 0.05)
    td_predict = make_predict(env_l, "td0")
    mc_predict = make_predict(env_l, "mc")
    v_td = td_predict(S_l, R_l, S_next_l, V0_l, alpha_l, 1.0)
    v_mc = mc_predict(S_l, G_l, S_next_l, V0_l, alpha_l, 1.0)

    td_l = rmse_over_states(v_td, v_true_l, ~env_l.terminal)[-1].mean()
    mc_l = rmse_over_states(v_mc, v_true_l, ~env_l.terminal)[-1].mean()
    print(f"{n_highway + 4:5d} {G_l[:, 0, :].std():10.2f} {td_l:8.3f} {mc_l:8.3f} {mc_l/td_l:7.2f}")

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Random Walk Problem
In this example, we have five states in a row with terminal absorbing states on both ends. We only receive a reward of \(+1\) for stepping off the right end, and we use a policy that flips a coin at every step. The exact values are \(v_\pi(i) = i/6\), which makes this a clean head-to-head comparison. In addition, we generate one set of episodes and hand the same episodes to both learners, so the comparison is paired and nothing is left to randomness about the data.

td0_walk = make_predict(walk5, "td0")
mc_walk = make_predict(walk5, "mc")

v_walk_true = np.arange(walk5.n_states) / 6.0
v_walk_true[6] = 0.0

inner_states = np.arange(1, 6)
pi_walk = np.ones((walk5.n_states, walk5.n_actions)) / walk5.n_actions

N_RUNS_WALK = 100
N_EPISODES_WALK = 100
MAX_STEPS_WALK = 80

alphas_td_walk = [0.05, 0.10, 0.15]
alphas_mc_walk = [0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.04]

def walk_experiment(predict, alphas):
    n_learners = N_RUNS_WALK * len(alphas)
    S, A, R, S_next, G, frac_finished = episodes_for(
        rollout_walk, walk5, pi_walk, N_EPISODES_WALK, n_learners, MAX_STEPS_WALK)
    V_init = np.full((n_learners, walk5.n_states), 0.5)
    V_init[:, [0, 6]] = 0.0
    targets = R if predict is td0_walk else G
    V = predict(S, targets, S_next, V_init, np.repeat(alphas, N_RUNS_WALK), 1.0)
    rmse = rmse_over_states(V, v_walk_true, inner_states)
    return V, {alpha: rmse[:, i * N_RUNS_WALK:(i + 1) * N_RUNS_WALK].mean(axis=1)
               for i, alpha in enumerate(alphas)}, frac_finished

V_walk_td, curves_td, frac_finished_td = walk_experiment(td0_walk, alphas_td_walk)
V_walk_mc, curves_mc, frac_finished_mc = walk_experiment(mc_walk, alphas_mc_walk)

We know that \(V(B) = \frac{3}{4}\) for both learners since six of the eight visits to B returned 1. But what is \(V(A)\)?

Batch Monte Carlo answers \(0\). The only return ever observed from A was 0, and 0 is the value that minimizes the squared error on the training set.
Batch TD(0) answers \(\frac{3}{4}\). A went to B 100% of the time with reward 0, so if we believe the process is Markov, \(v(A) = 0 + v(B) = \frac{3}{4}\).

TD’s answer is the one that generalizes because it converges to the certainty-equivalence estimate. Which is derived by building the maximum-likelihood MDP from the counts (observed transition frequencies and observed mean reward) and solving it exactly. Whereas, batch MC converges to the sample average of returns.
Below we compute the batch fixed points both ways by running the book’s sweeps, and by DP on the estimated model.

def make_batch_td(env, n_iters=500):
    """The batch-TD(0) fixed point, computed as policy evaluation on the maximum-likelihood
    model estimated from the batch.  Transitions arrive flat, (n_transitions, n_runs),
    weighted by weights."""
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    S = pt.lmatrix("S")
    R = pt.dmatrix("R")
    S_next = pt.lmatrix("Sp")
    weights = pt.dmatrix("W")
    gamma = pt.scalar("g")

    n_transitions, n_runs = S.shape[0], S.shape[1]
    run_of = pt.broadcast_to(pt.arange(n_runs), (n_transitions, n_runs)).ravel()

    s_flat, s_next_flat = S.ravel(), S_next.ravel()
    r_flat, w_flat = R.ravel(), weights.ravel()

    visits = pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros((n_runs, env.n_states))[run_of, s_flat], w_flat)
    reward_hat = pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros((n_runs, env.n_states))[run_of, s_flat], w_flat * r_flat)
    P_hat = pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros((n_runs, env.n_states, env.n_states))[run_of, s_flat, s_next_flat], w_flat)

    safe_visits = pt.switch(pt.gt(visits, 0), visits, 1.0)
    reward_hat = reward_hat / safe_visits # the max-likelihood model
    P_hat = P_hat / safe_visits[:, :, None]

    def evaluation_sweep(V, P_hat, reward_hat, gamma):
        return not_terminal[None, :] * (reward_hat + gamma * (P_hat * V[:, None, :]).sum(axis=2))

    # evaluated by DP
    V_iters = pytensor.scan(
        fn=evaluation_sweep,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((n_runs, env.n_states)),
        non_sequences=[P_hat, reward_hat, gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )

    return pytensor.function([S, R, S_next, weights, gamma], [V_iters[-1], visits, P_hat, reward_hat])

def make_batch_mc(env):
    "The batch-MC fixed point: the average observed return per state."
    S = pt.lmatrix("S")
    G = pt.dmatrix("G")
    weights = pt.dmatrix("W")

    n_transitions, n_runs = S.shape[0], S.shape[1]
    run_of = pt.broadcast_to(pt.arange(n_runs), (n_transitions, n_runs)).ravel()

    s_flat, g_flat, w_flat = S.ravel(), G.ravel(), weights.ravel()

    visits = pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros((n_runs, env.n_states))[run_of, s_flat], w_flat)
    return_total = pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros((n_runs, env.n_states))[run_of, s_flat], w_flat * g_flat)

    V_mc = return_total / pt.switch(pt.gt(visits, 0), visits, 1.0)

    return pytensor.function([S, G, weights], V_mc)


def make_batch_sweeps(env, kind):
    """increments summed over the whole batch with V
    held fixed, applied once per sweep, repeated until nothing moves."""
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    S = pt.lmatrix("S")
    targets = pt.dmatrix("X")
    S_next = pt.lmatrix("Sp")
    weights = pt.dmatrix("W")
    V_init = pt.dmatrix("V0")
    alpha = pt.scalar("alpha")
    gamma = pt.scalar("g")
    n_sweeps = pt.iscalar("K")

    n_transitions, n_runs = S.shape[0], S.shape[1]
    run_of = (pt.arange(n_runs)[None, :] * pt.ones((n_transitions, 1), dtype="int64")).ravel()
    s_flat, s_next_flat = S.ravel(), S_next.ravel()
    x_flat, w_flat = targets.ravel(), weights.ravel()

    def sweep(V, alpha, gamma):
        target = (x_flat + gamma * not_terminal[s_next_flat] * V[run_of, s_next_flat] if kind == "td0" else x_flat)

        increment = pt.inc_subtensor(pt.zeros_like(V)[run_of, s_flat],
                                     w_flat * (target - V[run_of, s_flat]))
        return V + alpha * increment

    V_sweeps = pytensor.scan(
        fn=sweep,
        outputs_info=V_init,
        non_sequences=[alpha, gamma],
        n_steps=n_sweeps,
        return_updates=False
    )

    return pytensor.function([S, targets, S_next, weights, V_init, alpha, gamma, n_sweeps],
                             V_sweeps, on_unused_input="ignore")


ab_env = make_env(

Batch TD has a lower error compared to batch MC. Even though batch MC is optimal on the training set. The reason is because minimizing in-sample error is the wrong objective if what you want is the value function of the underlying Markov process. Batch MC throws away the transition structure. Whereas batch TD is exactly DP applied to the best model of that structure you can build from the data, which is why it extrapolates to states whose returns you never observed.
However if the process is not Markov in the states, the certainty-equivalence estimate is fitting the wrong model, and TD’s advantage can disappear.

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Scan Implementation for Control Algorithms
Sarsa, Q-learning and Expected Sarsa differ only in how they compute the bootstrap term, so we build them from one factory function. The structure is a nested scan, and this time the environment lives inside the loop because the behavior depends on \(Q\), meaning it cannot be pre-generated:

inner scan one step of the agent’s life: draw \(S_{t+1}\) and \(R_{t+1}\), form the target, update \(Q\) with a batched inc_subtensor, pick the next action.
outer scan one episode: run T inner steps, then draw a fresh start state and first action.

Important implementation details:
A live flag (1 until the episode terminates, 0 after) multiplies \(\alpha\), so the fixed-length inner scan can pad past the end of a short episode without corrupting anything. eps_probs builds the \(\varepsilon\)-greedy distribution explicitly rather than sampling a coin flip, because Expected Sarsa needs those probabilities. Illegal actions get \(-\infty\) before the argmax and zero probability after it.
alpha and eps are vectors over the run dimension, which is how the step-size sweeps with just one batched call.

def make_control(env, kind, seed):
    """One-step tabular TD control.  kind = 'sarsa' | 'q' | 'expected_sarsa'.
    Returns f(Q_init, alpha, eps, gamma, n_episodes, max_steps) -> Q, reward sums, step
    counts, done flags, first action of each episode.  Q_init is (n_runs, n_states,
    n_actions); alpha and eps are (n_runs,)."""
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward_mean = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    reward_sd = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_sd)
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    start_dist = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.start)
    rng_shared = pt.random.shared_rng(seed=seed, name=f"rng_{kind}_{env.name}")

    Q_init = pt.dtensor3("Q0")
    alpha = pt.dvector("alpha")
    eps = pt.dvector("eps")
    gamma = pt.scalar("gamma")
    n_episodes = pt.iscalar("n_ep")
    max_steps = pt.iscalar("T")

    def eps_greedy_probs(Q, s, eps):
        "eps-greedy distribution over the legal actions of s, per run -> (n_runs, n_actions)"
        runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
        legal = legal_actions[s]
        greedy = pt.argmax(pt.where(legal > 0, Q[runs, s], NEG_INF), axis=1)
        probs = legal * (eps / legal.sum(axis=1))[:, None]
        return pt.inc_subtensor(probs[runs, greedy], 1.0 - eps)

    def pick(rng, Q, s, eps):
        return rng.categorical(p=eps_greedy_probs(Q, s, eps))

    def step(rng, s, a, Q, alpha, eps, gamma, still_running):
        "the shared half: take the step, then form the method's target"
        runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
        rng, s_next = rng.categorical(p=P[s, a])
        rng, r = rng.normal(loc=reward_mean[s, a], scale=reward_sd[s, a])

        if kind == "sarsa":
            rng, a_next = pick(rng, Q, s_next, eps) # A' chosen before the update
            bootstrap = Q[runs, s_next, a_next]
        elif kind == "q":
            a_next = None
            bootstrap = pt.where(legal_actions[s_next] > 0, Q[runs, s_next], NEG_INF).max(axis=1)
        else: # expected_sarsa
            a_next = None
            bootstrap = (eps_greedy_probs(Q, s_next, eps) * Q[runs, s_next]).sum(axis=1)

        delta = r + gamma * not_terminal[s_next] * bootstrap - Q[runs, s, a]
        Q_new = pt.inc_subtensor(Q[runs, s, a], alpha * still_running * delta)

        if a_next is None: # off-policy / expected target:
            rng, a_next = pick(rng, Q_new, s_next, eps) # next action from the new Q

        return rng, s_next, a_next, r, Q_new

    def inner(rng, s, a, still_running, Q, reward_sum, step_count, alpha, eps, gamma):
        rng, s_next, a_next, r, Q_new = step(rng, s, a, Q, alpha, eps, gamma, still_running)
        return (rng, s_next, a_next, still_running * not_terminal[s_next], Q_new,
                reward_sum + still_running * r, step_count + still_running)

    def episode(rng, s, a, Q, alpha, eps, gamma, max_steps):
        zero = pt.zeros_like(not_terminal[s])

        rng_final, S_seq, A_seq, running_seq, Q_seq, reward_sum, step_count = pytensor.scan(
            fn=inner,
            outputs_info=[rng, s, a, zero + 1.0, Q, zero, zero],
            non_sequences=[alpha, eps, gamma],
            n_steps=max_steps,
            return_updates=False
        )

        Q_new = Q_seq[-1]
        rng, s_new = rng_final.categorical(p=pt.ones((Q.shape[0], 1)) * start_dist[None, :])
        rng, a_new = pick(rng, Q_new, s_new, eps)
        return rng, s_new, a_new, Q_new, reward_sum[-1], step_count[-1], 1.0 - running_seq[-1]

    rng_a, s_first = rng_shared.categorical(p=pt.ones((Q_init.shape[0], 1)) * start_dist[None, :])
    rng_b, a_first = pick(rng_a, Q_init, s_first, eps)

    rng_final, S_out, A_out, Q_out, reward_sum, step_count, done = pytensor.scan(
        fn=episode,
        outputs_info=[rng_b, s_first, a_first, Q_init, None, None, None],
        non_sequences=[alpha, eps, gamma, max_steps],
        n_steps=n_episodes,
        return_updates=False
    )

    first_action = pt.concatenate([a_first[None, :], A_out[:-1]], axis=0)

    return pytensor.function([Q_init, alpha, eps, gamma, n_episodes, max_steps],
                             [Q_out[-1], reward_sum, step_count, done, first_action],
                             updates={rng_shared: rng_final})


def eps_greedy_pi(Q, eps, env):
    "the eps-greedy policy of a Q table, as an (n_states, n_actions) matrix for the DP oracle"
    legal = env.legal_actions > 0
    pi = legal * (eps / legal.sum(axis=1))[:, None]
    pi[np.arange(env.n_states), np.where(legal, Q, NEG_INF).argmax(axis=1)] += 1 - eps
    return pi

def greedy_pi(Q, env):
    pi = np.zeros((env.n_states, env.n_actions))
    pi[np.arange(env.n_states),
       np.where(env.legal_actions > 0, Q, NEG_INF).argmax(axis=1)] = 1.0
    return pi

def value_gap(Q, env, gamma=1.0):
    "how far the greedy policy of Q is from optimal, measured exactly by DP"
    evaluate_policy, optimal_values, _ = ORACLE[env.name]
    graded_states = env.reachable & ~env.terminal
    return np.abs(evaluate_policy(greedy_pi(Q, env), gamma) - optimal_values(gamma))[graded_states].max()

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Windy Gridworld
An upward wind can push the agent up 1-2 cells, depending on the column you are leaving. Every step costs \(-1\), so the task is to reach the goal quickly. The shortest route is 15 steps to the goal.
MC control would struggle on this environment because with an undiscounted, purely negative reward per step and a policy that has not yet found the goal, episodes can run for thousands of steps and an MC method learns nothing at all until an episode ends. Whereas Sarsa improves its policy mid-episode, which is why the first episode below takes ~900 steps and the twentieth takes ~70.
A steeper slope in the plot below signifies shorter episodes.

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Cliff Walking
The point of the cliff is that the optimal path and the safe path differ. The shortest route runs along the very edge of the cliff. Notice though, that with \(\varepsilon=0.1\) that route also means a one-in-ten chance per step of being blown into the cliff for \(-100\) reward.

Q-learning learns the values of the optimal path and falls into the cliff regularly. Its online return is the worst of the three learners even though its \(Q\) is the most correct.
Sarsa learns the values of its own \(\varepsilon\)-greedy behavior, which include the cliff risk, so it backs off to a safer route and earns more per episode.

That is the on-policy/off-policy distinction paying a visible dividend, in both directions.

N_EPISODES_CLIFF = 500
MAX_STEPS_CLIFF = 200

        np.zeros((N_RUNS_CLIFF, cliff.n_states, cliff.n_actions)),
        np.full(N_RUNS_CLIFF, 0.5),
        np.full(N_RUNS_CLIFF, 0.1),
        GAMMA,
        N_EPISODES_CLIFF,
        MAX_STEPS_CLIFF

Q-learning matches \(q_*\). \(Q(\text{start}) = -13.00\) is exactly the optimal action value, even though every episode was generated by an \(\varepsilon\)-greedy policy that keeps falling off the cliff. Due to learning using an off-policy framework, we evaluate the greedy policy, the \(\max_a\) in the target, while the agent behaves according to its own behavior policy which gets estimated poorly at \(q_{\pi_\varepsilon}(\text{start}) = -45.78\). This is why the online return in the figure above is worse than Sarsa’s even though its value estimates are better.
Sarsa and Expected Sarsa match \(q_{\pi_\varepsilon}\), the value of the policy they actually follow. Their \(\approx5\) gap to \(q_*\) is the price of 10% exploration

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
Utilities & Environment Setup
A hands-on companion to Chapter 7 of Sutton & Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction.
In the previous chapter we learned about methods that bootstrap off of a one-step lookahead of the next state, and prior to that we looked at Monte Carlo methods that didn’t bootstrap at all, hence, needing to wait until the end of an episode to learn anything. In this chapter, we look at methods that are intermediary between those two extremes.
Specifically, we look \(n\) steps ahead and bootstrap off the state you find there:
\[
G_{t:t+n} \doteq R_{t+1} + \gamma R_{t+2} + \cdots + \gamma^{n-1}R_{t+n} + \gamma^{n}V_{t+n-1}(S_{t+n})
\]
Notice that when \(n = 1\), we get back TD(0), and when \(n \ge T-t\) we get back the Monte Carlo return.
Everything in between is what we will be working through in this chapter.
As with everything, there is no free-lunch. The \(n\)-step return is not available until time \(t+n\), so the update
\[
V_{t+n}(S_t) \doteq V_{t+n-1}(S_t) + \alpha\left[G_{t:t+n} - V_{t+n-1}(S_t)\right]
\]
is applied \(n\) steps late, and the first \(n-1\) steps of an episode make no update at all.
We will work through every section of the chapter including:
Four environments are used in this chapter:
All are finite MDPs, so we can always compute the exact answer with dynamic programming and grade the learner against it.

As we have done in prior chapters we will have one container hold everything that an algorithm might need.

NEG_INF = -1e30   # stand-in for -inf when masking illegal actions

@dataclass
class Env:
    name: str
    n_states: int
    n_actions: int
    P: np.ndarray              # (n_states, n_actions, n_states) transition probabilities
    reward_mean: np.ndarray    # (n_states, n_actions)
    reward_sd: np.ndarray      # (n_states, n_actions)
    terminal: np.ndarray       # (n_states,) bool
    start: np.ndarray          # (n_states,) start-state distribution
    legal_actions: np.ndarray  # (n_states, n_actions) 1.0 where the action is allowed
    reachable: np.ndarray      # (n_states,) reachable from a start state
    shape: tuple = ()          # grid shape, for printing


def make_env(name, n_states, n_actions, step_fn, terminals, starts, shape=(), legal_actions=None):
    "step_fn(s, a) returns (s_next, reward_mean, reward_sd); terminals absorb with reward 0."
    P = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions, n_states))
    reward_mean = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    reward_sd = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    terminal = np.zeros(n_states, dtype=bool); terminal[list(terminals)] = True

    for s in range(n_states):
        for a in range(n_actions):
            if terminal[s]:
                P[s, a, s] = 1.0
                continue
            s_next, mean, sd = step_fn(s, a)
            P[s, a, s_next] = 1.0
            reward_mean[s, a] = mean
            reward_sd[s, a] = sd

    start = np.zeros(n_states)
    start[list(starts)] = 1.0 / len(list(starts))

    if legal_actions is None:
        legal_actions = np.ones((n_states, n_actions))

    reachable = start > 0 # Breadth-First-Search over the legal actions
    legal_P = P * (legal_actions > 0)[:, :, None] # illegal (s, a) rows zeroed out
    while True:
        frontier = legal_P[reachable & ~terminal] # transitions out of reachable, non-terminal states
        one_step_reachable = frontier.sum(axis=(0, 1)) > 0
        grown = reachable | one_step_reachable
        if grown.sum() == reachable.sum(): # No new states are reachable
            break
        reachable = grown

    return Env(name, n_states, n_actions, P, reward_mean, reward_sd, terminal, start,
               legal_actions, reachable, shape)


UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT = 0, 1, 2, 3
ARROWS = {UP: "^", DOWN: "v", LEFT: "<", RIGHT: ">"}
STEP = {UP: (0, 1), DOWN: (0, -1), LEFT: (-1, 0), RIGHT: (1, 0)}   # action -> (dx, dy) when drawn

def _move(row, col, action, n_rows, n_cols):
    if action == UP: row = max(row - 1, 0)
    elif action == DOWN: row = min(row + 1, n_rows - 1)
    elif action == LEFT: col = max(col - 1, 0)
    elif action == RIGHT: col = min(col + 1, n_cols - 1)
    return row, col

def show_grid(values, env, title="", fmt="6.1f"):
    if title: print(title)
    n_rows, n_cols = env.shape
    for row in np.asarray(values, dtype=float).reshape(n_rows, n_cols):
        print("  " + "  ".join(f"{x:{fmt}}" for x in row))

def show_policy(actions, env, title="", extra=None):
    "extra: dict cell -> character, drawn on top (terminals, goal, start, ...)"
    if title: print(title)
    n_rows, n_cols = env.shape
    chars = [ARROWS[int(a)] for a in actions]
    for s in np.flatnonzero(env.terminal): chars[s] = "T"
    for s in np.flatnonzero(~env.reachable): chars[s] = "."
    for s, ch in (extra or {}).items(): chars[s] = ch
    for row in range(n_rows):
        print("   " + " ".join(chars[row * n_cols:(row + 1) * n_cols]))

The four environments. All are undiscounted (\(\gamma = 1\)).

walk19: Nineteen states in a row, absorbing on both ends, \(-1\) for stepping off the left end and \(+1\) off the right, always starting in the centre.
room: A \(6\times10\) open room, every reward \(0\) except \(+1\) for reaching the goal in the top-right corner.
windy: a \(7\times10\) grid with an upward wind of 0-2 cells depending on the column you leave from, \(-1\) per step.
cliff: a \(4\times12\) grid where stepping into the bottom-row cliff costs \(-100\) and teleports you back to the start.


def walk_env(n_walk=19):
    """A random walk on n_walk states in a row with absorbing ends: -1 for stepping off the
    left end, +1 off the right, 0 everywhere else, always starting in the middle."""
    n_states = n_walk + 2
    def step(s, a): # a = 0 left, a = 1 right
        s_next = s - 1 if a == 0 else s + 1
        return s_next, (-1.0 if s_next == 0 else 1.0 if s_next == n_states - 1 else 0.0), 0.0
    return make_env(f"walk{n_walk}", n_states, 2, step, [0, n_states - 1],
                    [(n_states - 1) // 2], shape=(1, n_states))

def room_env(n_rows=6, n_cols=10):
    """Figure 7.4's board: an open room, every reward 0 except +1 for reaching the goal in the
    top-right corner. Until an episode reaches G there is nothing at all to learn."""
    goal = n_cols - 1
    start = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols
    def step(s, a):
        row, col = _move(*divmod(s, n_cols), a, n_rows, n_cols)
        s_next = row * n_cols + col
        return s_next, (1.0 if s_next == goal else 0.0), 0.0
    return make_env("room", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [goal], [start], shape=(n_rows, n_cols))


WIND = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0])

def windy_env(n_rows=7, n_cols=10):
    def step(s, a):
        row, col = divmod(s, n_cols)
        row_next, col_next = _move(row, col, a, n_rows, n_cols)
        row_next = max(row_next - WIND[col], 0)   # wind of the column you leave, blowing up
        return row_next * n_cols + col_next, -1.0, 0.0
    return make_env("windy", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [3 * n_cols + 7], [3 * n_cols],
                    shape=(n_rows, n_cols))

def cliff_env(n_rows=4, n_cols=12):
    start_state = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols
    goal = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols + n_cols - 1
    cliff_cells = {(n_rows - 1) * n_cols + col for col in range(1, n_cols - 1)}
    def step(s, a):
        row, col = _move(*divmod(s, n_cols), a, n_rows, n_cols)
        s_next = row * n_cols + col
        return (start_state, -100.0, 0.0) if s_next in cliff_cells else (s_next, -1.0, 0.0)
    return make_env("cliff", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [goal], [start_state],
                    shape=(n_rows, n_cols))

walk19, room, windy, cliff = walk_env(19), room_env(), windy_env(), cliff_env()

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
The DP oracle
The same DP Oracle deal we have been implementing across the last few chapters.

def make_dp(env, n_iters=2000):
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    gamma = pt.scalar("gamma")
    pi = pt.matrix("pi")
    v_in = pt.vector("v")

    def q_from(v, gamma):
        return reward + gamma * (P * v[None, None, :]).sum(axis=2)

    def expectation_step(v, pi, gamma): # v_{k+1}(s) = sum_a pi(a|s) q_k(s, a)
        return not_terminal * (pi * q_from(v, gamma)).sum(axis=1)

    def optimality_step(v, gamma): # v_{k+1}(s) = max over the legal a of q_k(s, a)
        q = pt.where(legal_actions > 0, q_from(v, gamma), NEG_INF)
        return not_terminal * q.max(axis=1)

    v_eval = pytensor.scan(
        fn=expectation_step,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((env.n_states,)),
        non_sequences=[pi, gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )

    v_star = pytensor.scan(
        fn=optimality_step,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((env.n_states,)),
        non_sequences=[gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )
    return (pytensor.function([pi, gamma], v_eval[-1]), # evaluate_policy
            pytensor.function([gamma], v_star[-1]), # optimal_values
            pytensor.function([v_in, gamma], q_from(v_in, gamma))) # action_values_of


ORACLE = {e.name: make_dp(e) for e in (walk19, room, windy, cliff)}

def exact(env, gamma=1.0, pi=None):
    "v_pi if a policy is given, else v_*; always with the matching action values."
    evaluate_policy, optimal_values, action_values_of = ORACLE[env.name]
    v = evaluate_policy(pi, gamma) if pi is not None else optimal_values(gamma)
    q = action_values_of(v, gamma)
    q[env.terminal] = 0.0
    return v, q

def greedy_pi(Q, env):
    pi = np.zeros((env.n_states, env.n_actions))
    pi[np.arange(env.n_states),
       np.where(env.legal_actions > 0, Q, NEG_INF).argmax(axis=1)] = 1.0
    return pi

inner_states = np.arange(1, 20)                       # the 19 non-terminal walk states
pi_walk = np.ones((walk19.n_states, 2)) / 2           # the equiprobable random policy
v_walk, _ = exact(walk19, 1.0, pi_walk)

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
Simulator
Again same deal as before but now we need to pay a little more attention to the padding.
That padding does more work in this chapter than it did in the last one. An \(n\)-step window that starts before the episode ends will often extend past it, and the book handles this by truncating the return at \(T\). We get the same thing for free: past \(T\) the rewards are 0 and the bootstrap term is multiplied by \(\mathrm{not\_terminal}\), so \(G_{t:t+n}\) silently collapses to the full return \(G_t\) - with no special case in the code. The one thing we owe it is enough room: episodes must finish at least \(n\) steps before max_steps, and every experiment below reports what fraction actually did.

def make_rollout(env, seed):
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward_mean = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    reward_sd = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_sd)
    rng_shared = pt.random.shared_rng(seed=seed, name=f"rng_roll_{env.name}")
    pi = pt.matrix("pi")
    s_start = pt.lvector("s0")
    max_steps = pt.iscalar("T")

    def step(s, rng, pi):
        rng, a = rng.categorical(p=pi[s]) # A_t ~ b(.|S_t)
        rng, s_next = rng.categorical(p=P[s, a]) # S_{t+1} ~ p(.|S_t,A_t)
        rng, r = rng.normal(loc=reward_mean[s, a], scale=reward_sd[s, a]) # R_{t+1}
        return s_next, rng, a, r

    S_next, rng_final, A, R = pytensor.scan(
        fn=step,
        outputs_info=[s_start, rng_shared, None, None],
        non_sequences=[pi],
        n_steps=max_steps,
        return_updates=False
    )
    S = pt.concatenate([s_start[None, :], S_next[:-1]], axis=0) # row t = S_t
    return pytensor.function([pi, s_start, max_steps], [S, A, R, S_next],
                             updates={rng_shared: rng_final})

def episodes_for(rollout, env, b, n_episodes, n_learners, max_steps, pi=None):
    """One rollout call under the behavior policy b, reshaped into
    (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners) so learner r sees its own stream of episodes in order.
    rho is pi(A|S)/b(A|S), and 1 on the padded steps past termination."""
    n_chains = n_episodes * n_learners
    s_start = np_rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(env.start > 0), size=n_chains,
                            p=env.start[env.start > 0]).astype("int64")
    S, A, R, S_next = rollout(b, s_start, max_steps)
    by_episode = lambda X: X.reshape(max_steps, n_episodes, n_learners).transpose(1, 0, 2)
    S, A, R = by_episode(S), by_episode(A), by_episode(R)
    rho = np.ones_like(R) if pi is None else pi[S, A] / b[S, A]
    rho[env.terminal[S]] = 1.0
    return S, A, R, rho, env.terminal[S_next[-1]].mean()

np_rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
rollout_walk = make_rollout(walk19, 2026)

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
The update as a scan
The book’s pseudocode keeps a rolling buffer of the last \(n\) states and rewards and, at each step \(t\), updates the state \(\tau = t - n + 1\). When the transitions are already recorded there is no buffer to manage: pytensor.scan walks \(\tau\) itself and slices the window \(S_\tau\ldots S_{\tau+n}\), \(R_{\tau+1}\ldots R_{\tau+n}\) straight out of the episode, stopping at \(\tau = T - n\) rather than running off the end of the array.
The V carried through the scan at iteration \(\tau\) is the one produced by all the updates for \(\tau' < \tau\), which are the updates made at times up to \(\tau + n - 1\). That is exactly the book’s \(V_{t+n-1}\), so the online character of the algorithm is preserved rather than approximated.

def make_n_step_predict(env, n, kind="on_policy"):
    """n-step TD prediction.  kind = 'on_policy' | 'importance_sampling' | 'control_variates'.
    Episodes arrive as (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners); V comes back after every episode.
    alpha is an (n_learners,) vector, which is how the step-size sweeps run as one call."""
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    S_all = pt.ltensor3("S")
    R_all = pt.dtensor3("R")
    rho_all = pt.dtensor3("rho")
    V_init = pt.dmatrix("V0")
    alpha = pt.dvector("alpha")
    gamma = pt.scalar("g")
    gamma_pow = (gamma ** pt.arange(n + 1))[:, None] # gamma^0 .. gamma^n

    def transition(tau, V, S_ep, R_ep, rho_ep, alpha, gamma, gamma_pow):
        """The update at time tau.  The window is sliced out of the episode, and the return over it
        is scanned rather than unrolled, so the graph is the same size whatever n is."""
        S_win = S_ep[tau:tau + n + 1] # S_tau .. S_{tau+n}, (n+1, n_learners)
        R_win = R_ep[tau:tau + n] # R_{tau+1} .. R_{tau+n}, (n, n_learners)
        rho_win = rho_ep[tau:tau + n] # rho_tau .. rho_{tau+n-1}, (n, n_learners)

        learners = pt.arange(V.shape[0])
        V_win = not_terminal[S_win] * V[learners, S_win]  # V(S_tau..S_{tau+n}), 0 at terminals
        s_tau = S_win[0]
        still_running = not_terminal[s_tau] # no update once the episode has ended

        if kind == "control_variates":

            def down_one_level(rho_j, R_j, V_j, G, gamma):
                "G_{j:h} = rho_j (R_{j+1} + gamma G_{j+1:h}) + (1 - rho_j) V(S_j)"
                return rho_j * (R_j + gamma * G) + (1 - rho_j) * V_j

            G_levels = pytensor.scan( # from the base case back up to tau
                fn=down_one_level,
                sequences=[rho_win[::-1], R_win[::-1], V_win[:n][::-1]],
                outputs_info=V_win[n], # G_{h:h} = V(S_h)
                non_sequences=[gamma],
                return_updates=False)
            G, weight = G_levels[-1], 1.0
        else:
            G = (gamma_pow[:n] * R_win).sum(axis=0) + gamma_pow[n] * V_win[n]
            weight = rho_win.prod(axis=0) if kind == "importance_sampling" else 1.0

        return pt.inc_subtensor(V[learners, s_tau],
                                alpha * still_running * weight * (G - V[learners, s_tau]))

    def episode(S_ep, R_ep, rho_ep, V, alpha, gamma, gamma_pow):
        V_steps = pytensor.scan(
            fn=transition,
            sequences=pt.arange(S_ep.shape[0] - n), # tau = 0 .. max_steps-n-1
            outputs_info=V,
            non_sequences=[S_ep, R_ep, rho_ep, alpha, gamma, gamma_pow],
            return_updates=False
        )
        return V_steps[-1]

    V_per_episode = pytensor.scan(
        fn=episode,
        sequences=[S_all, R_all, rho_all],
        outputs_info=V_init,
        non_sequences=[alpha, gamma, gamma_pow],
        return_updates=False
    )
    return pytensor.function([S_all, R_all, rho_all, V_init, alpha, gamma], V_per_episode)

One-step TD moves exactly one state per episode. The reward is non-zero only at the two ends, so \(n=1\) leaves 18 of the 19 states at zero after the first episode. \(n=16\) moves seven states, and moves them toward the oracle value. This is why \(n\)-step methods learn faster early.
Every curve is a U in \(\alpha\), and the best \(\alpha\) falls as \(n\) grows. A larger \(n\) means the target sums more sampled rewards, so it carries more variance, so it can tolerate a smaller step.
The best \(n\) is in the middle.

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
The scan update for control
Now that the behavior policy depends on \(Q\), we can no longer pre-generate the whole episode and just slice through it. Instead, we keep a rolling buffer of three arrays \((S, A, R)\) of shape (n_runs, n) that slide one column per step, ensuring that after the step at time \(t\) they hold \(S_\tau\ldots S_{t}\), \(A_\tau\ldots A_t\) and \(R_{\tau+1}\ldots R_{t+1}\) for \(\tau = t-n+1\). That is one column short of the window: the live pair \((S_{t+1}, A_{t+1})\) supplies \(S_{\tau+n}\) and \(A_{\tau+n}\), which is why \(A_{t+1}\) is drawn before the update fires.
The buffers are initialised to a terminal state, so the mask that suppresses updates past the end of an episode also suppresses the first \(n-1\) steps, when the window has not yet filled. Every \(Q\) term in each return is read off the current \(Q\), which corresponds to the book’s \(Q_{\tau+n-1}\).
The following sections differ only in the return, so we write the returns once, as a single function, and let the control loop stay fixed. Only the first two branches are used in this section.

def eps_greedy_probs(env, Q, s, eps):
    "eps-greedy distribution over the legal actions of s, per run -> (..., n_runs, n_actions)"
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
    legal = legal_actions[s]
    greedy = pt.argmax(pt.where(legal > 0, Q[runs, s], NEG_INF), axis=-1)
    probs = legal * (eps / legal.sum(axis=-1))[..., None]
    one_hot = pt.eq(pt.arange(legal.shape[-1]), greedy[..., None])
    return probs + one_hot * (1.0 - eps)[:, None]


def n_step_return(env, kind, n, Q, S_win, A_win, R_win, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma):
    """action-value returns over one window.

    S_win / A_win are the stacked windows S_tau..S_{tau+n} and A_tau..A_{tau+n} (n+1, n_runs),
    and R_win is R_{tau+1}..R_{tau+n}, (n, n_runs).  Every Q term is read off
    the current Q, which is the book's Q_{h-1}. Returns (G, weight)

    kind = 'sarsa' gamma^n Q(S_{tau+n}, A_{tau+n})
           'expected_sarsa' + gamma^n V-bar(S_{tau+n})
           'off_policy_sarsa' the same G, scaled by rho_{tau+1:tau+n}
           'q_sigma' sigma = 0 -> tree backup,
                     sigma = 1 -> per-decision control variates

    """
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
    gamma_pow = (gamma ** pt.arange(n + 1))[:, None]

    def at(s, a):
        live = not_terminal[s]
        pi_probs = eps_greedy_probs(env, Q, s, eps_target)
        b_probs = eps_greedy_probs(env, Q, s, eps_behavior)
        take = lambda probs: pt.take_along_axis(probs, a[..., None], axis=-1)[..., 0]
        pi_a = take(pi_probs)
        pi_b = take(b_probs)
        return dict(
            q=live * Q[runs, s, a], # Q(S, A)
            q_bar=live * (pi_probs * Q[runs, s]).sum(axis=-1), # V-bar(S)
            pi_a=pi_a, # pi(A | S)
            rho=1.0 + live * (pi_a / pi_b - 1.0)) # 1 when not live and minus 1 to counter the added 1

    if kind == "q_sigma":
        step = at(S_win[1:], A_win[1:]) # levels tau+1 .. tau+n, valued in one go
        c = sigma * step["rho"] + (1 - sigma) * step["pi_a"]  # control variate

        def down_one_level(R_j, c_j, q_j, q_bar_j, G, gamma):
            "G_{j-1} = R_j + gamma c_j (G_j - Q(S_j, A_j)) + gamma V-bar(S_j)"
            return R_j + gamma * c_j * (G - q_j) + gamma * q_bar_j

        G_levels = pytensor.scan(
            fn=down_one_level,
            sequences=[R_win[::-1], c[::-1], step["q"][::-1], step["q_bar"][::-1]],
            outputs_info=step["q"][n - 1],  # G_{h:h} = Q(S_h, A_h)
            non_sequences=[gamma],
            return_updates=False)
        return G_levels[-1], 1.0

    if kind == "off_policy_sarsa":
        step = at(S_win[1:], A_win[1:])
        bootstrap, weight = step["q"][n - 1], step["rho"].prod(axis=0) # rho_{tau+1:tau+n}
    else:
        step = at(S_win[n], A_win[n])
        bootstrap = step["q_bar"] if kind == "expected_sarsa" else step["q"]
        weight = 1.0

    return (gamma_pow[:n] * R_win).sum(axis=0) + gamma_pow[n] * bootstrap, weight


def make_n_step_control(env, kind, n, seed):
    """n-step tabular TD control.  behavior is eps_behavior-greedy in Q and the target policy
    is eps_target-greedy in Q, so equal epsilons make every method on-policy.  

    alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target and sigma are (n_runs,) vectors, which is how the sweeps below
    run many settings as one batched call."""
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward_mean = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    reward_sd = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_sd)
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    start_dist = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.start)
    pad_state = int(np.argmax(env.terminal))   # buffer filler: masks the first n-1 updates
    rng_shared = pt.random.shared_rng(seed=seed, name=f"rng_{kind}{n}_{env.name}")

    Q_init = pt.dtensor3("Q0")
    alpha = pt.dvector("alpha")
    eps_behavior = pt.dvector("eps_b")
    eps_target = pt.dvector("eps_pi")
    sigma = pt.dvector("sigma")
    gamma = pt.scalar("gamma")
    n_episodes = pt.iscalar("n_ep")
    max_steps = pt.iscalar("T")

    def pick(rng, Q, s, eps):
        return rng.categorical(p=eps_greedy_probs(env, Q, s, eps))

    def shift_in(buffer, x):
        "drop the oldest column and append x - the window slides one step"
        return pt.concatenate([buffer[:, 1:], x[:, None]], axis=1)

    def inner(rng, s, a, live, S_buf, A_buf, R_buf, Q, reward_sum, step_count,
              alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma):
        runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
        rng, s_next = rng.categorical(p=P[s, a])
        rng, r = rng.normal(loc=reward_mean[s, a], scale=reward_sd[s, a])
        rng, a_next = pick(rng, Q, s_next, eps_behavior)   # A_{t+1}, drawn before the update

        S_buf, A_buf, R_buf = shift_in(S_buf, s), shift_in(A_buf, a), shift_in(R_buf, r)
        S_win = pt.concatenate([S_buf.T, s_next[None]])     # S_tau .. S_{tau+n}, (n+1, n_runs)
        A_win = pt.concatenate([A_buf.T, a_next[None]])     # A_tau .. A_{tau+n}
        R_win = R_buf.T                                     # R_{tau+1} .. R_{tau+n}, (n, n_runs)

        G, weight = n_step_return(env, kind, n, Q, S_win, A_win, R_win,
                                  eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma)
        s_tau, a_tau = S_win[0], A_win[0]
        updates = not_terminal[s_tau]   # 0 while the window is still filling, and past T
        Q = pt.inc_subtensor(Q[runs, s_tau, a_tau],
                             alpha * updates * weight * (G - Q[runs, s_tau, a_tau]))

        return (rng, s_next, a_next, live * not_terminal[s_next], S_buf, A_buf, R_buf, Q,
                reward_sum + live * r, step_count + live)

    def episode(rng, s, a, Q, alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, max_steps):
        zero = pt.zeros_like(not_terminal[s])
        n_runs = Q.shape[0]
        pad = pt.zeros((n_runs, n), dtype="int64")

        (rng_final, S_seq, A_seq, live_seq, _, _, _, Q_seq,
         reward_sum, step_count) = pytensor.scan(
            fn=inner,
            outputs_info=[
                rng,
                s,
                a,
                zero + 1.0,
                pad + pad_state,
                pad,
                pt.zeros((n_runs, n)),
                Q,
                zero,
                zero
            ],
            non_sequences=[alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma],
            n_steps=max_steps,
            return_updates=False
        )

        Q_new = Q_seq[-1]
        rng, s_new = rng_final.categorical(p=pt.ones((n_runs, 1)) * start_dist[None, :])
        rng, a_new = pick(rng, Q_new, s_new, eps_behavior)
        return rng, s_new, a_new, Q_new, reward_sum[-1], step_count[-1], 1.0 - live_seq[-1]

    rng_a, s_first = rng_shared.categorical(p=pt.ones((Q_init.shape[0], 1)) * start_dist[None, :])
    rng_b, a_first = pick(rng_a, Q_init, s_first, eps_behavior)

    rng_final, S_out, A_out, Q_out, reward_sum, step_count, done = pytensor.scan(
        fn=episode,
        outputs_info=[rng_b, s_first, a_first, Q_init, None, None, None],
        non_sequences=[alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, max_steps],
        n_steps=n_episodes,
        return_updates=False
    )

    return pytensor.function(
        [Q_init, alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, n_episodes, max_steps],
        [Q_out[-1], reward_sum, step_count, done],
        updates={rng_shared: rng_final}, on_unused_input="ignore")

Using the open room environment we show a similar idea as the Random Walk example, where the one-step Sarsa can only update one action value compared to ten action values with 10-step Sarsa

path_A = A_room[:T_room, chosen]

def n_step_sarsa_one_episode(n, alpha=ALPHA_ROOM, gamma=1.0):
    "Sutton & Barto's n-step Sarsa pseudocode, written out for a single recorded episode. Policy Evaluation only."
    Q = np.zeros((room.n_states, room.n_actions))
    for tau in range(T_room):
        horizon = min(tau + n, T_room)
        G = sum(gamma ** (k - tau) * path_R[k] for k in range(tau, horizon))
        if tau + n < T_room: # bootstrap only if the horizon is inside the episode
            G += gamma ** n * Q[path_S[tau + n], path_A[tau + n]]
        Q[path_S[tau], path_A[tau]] += alpha * (G - Q[path_S[tau], path_A[tau]])
    return Q

Notice how the learner doubles back on itself in 10-step Sarsa, so the ten strengthened pairs sit in nine distinct cells, and the cell the path crossed twice has two of its actions updated.
Those ten values are now non-zero, so the next episode has something to bootstrap from as soon as it enters that neighborhood. Remember this doesn’t come for free, though. Those ten targets are the true return over ten sampled steps, and on a stochastic problem that is ten steps worth of noise.

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
Windy gridworld control
We sweep \(n\) and \(\alpha\) together and count the total time steps needed for 170 episodes. This allows us to measure of how fast the policy improves.

N_RUNS_WINDY, N_EPISODES_WINDY, MAX_STEPS_WINDY = 30, 170, 1200
alphas_windy = np.round(np.arange(0.1, 0.91, 0.1), 2)
n_values_windy = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]

n_learners_windy = N_RUNS_WINDY * len(alphas_windy)
repeat_windy = lambda x: np.full(n_learners_windy, float(x))
Q_init_windy = np.zeros((n_learners_windy, windy.n_states, windy.n_actions))
v_star_windy, _ = exact(windy)
start_windy = int(np.argmax(windy.start))

steps_windy = {}
for n in n_values_windy:
    learner = make_n_step_control(windy, "sarsa", n, n)
    Q, reward_sum, step_count, done = learner(
        Q_init_windy,
        np.repeat(alphas_windy, N_RUNS_WINDY),
        repeat_windy(0.1),
        repeat_windy(0.1),
        repeat_windy(1.0),
        1.0,
        N_EPISODES_WINDY,
        MAX_STEPS_WINDY
    )
    steps_windy[n] = step_count.sum(axis=0).reshape(len(alphas_windy), N_RUNS_WINDY).mean(axis=1)


windy_fig = go.Figure()

for i, (n, curve) in enumerate(steps_windy.items()):
    windy_fig.add_scatter(
        x=alphas_windy,
        y=curve,
        mode="lines+markers",
        name=f"n={n}",
        line=dict(color=colors[i], width=2),
        marker=dict(size=7, line=dict(color="white", width=1)),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{y:.0f}</b> time steps"
    )

windy_fig.add_hline(
    y=-v_star_windy[start_windy] * N_EPISODES_WINDY,
    line=dict(color="grey", width=1, dash="dash"),
    annotation_text=f"optimal ({-v_star_windy[start_windy]:.0f} steps/episode, if you never explore)",
    annotation_position="bottom right"
)

windy_fig.update_layout(
    title="<b>n-step Sarsa on the windy gridworld</b>"
          f"<br><sup>time steps to complete {N_EPISODES_WINDY} episodes, "
          f"{N_RUNS_WINDY} runs per point, eps = 0.1</sup>",
    xaxis_title=r"$\alpha$",
    yaxis=dict(title="total time steps"),
    template="plotly_white",
    hovermode="x unified",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.0, x=0),
    margin=dict(t=100, b=100)
)

windy_fig.show(config=dict(displayModeBar=False))

                            
                                            



windy_fig = go.Figure()

for i, (n, curve) in enumerate(steps_windy.items()):
    windy_fig.add_scatter(
        x=alphas_windy,
        y=curve,
        mode="lines+markers",
        name=f"n={n}",
        line=dict(color=colors[i], width=2),
        marker=dict(size=7, line=dict(color="white", width=1)),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{y:.0f}</b> time steps"
    )

windy_fig.add_hline(
    y=-v_star_windy[start_windy] * N_EPISODES_WINDY,
    line=dict(color="grey", width=1, dash="dash"),
    annotation_text=f"optimal ({-v_star_windy[start_windy]:.0f} steps/episode, if you never explore)",
    annotation_position="bottom right"
)

windy_fig.update_layout(
    title="<b>n-step Sarsa on the windy gridworld</b>"
          f"<br><sup>time steps to complete {N_EPISODES_WINDY} episodes, "
          f"{N_RUNS_WINDY} runs per point, eps = 0.1</sup>",
    xaxis_title=r"$\alpha$",
    yaxis=dict(title="total time steps"),
    template="plotly_dark",
    hovermode="x unified",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.0, x=0),
    margin=dict(t=100, b=100)
)

Past \(n=4\), learning degrades badly because on the windy gridworld the early episodes are wandering randomly for hundreds of steps, and a long \(n\)-step return computed from a near-random trajectory is mostly noise about a policy that no longer exists by the time the update is applied.

title: Planning and Learning with Tabular Methods
text:
Utilities & Environment Setup
A hands-on companion to Chapter 8 of Sutton & Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction.
So far the book has given us two families of methods that look quite different:
This chapter brings the two together. Its main claim is that both families do the same thing. Each one estimates a value function by backing up values, using the values of the states that can come next to improve the value of the current one, and then acts on those values:
\[
\text{model} \longrightarrow \text{simulated experience} \xrightarrow{\text{backups}} \text{values} \longrightarrow \text{policy}
\]
The only difference is where the experience comes from. When it is real, collected by acting in the world, we call the process learning. When it is simulated, generated by a model, we call it planning. Any learning update becomes a planning method as soon as we feed it simulated experience, and nothing stops one agent from doing both at once.
We work through the following topics:
We finish with a summary and recap.
As in the previous chapters, every environment here is a finite MDP: a problem small enough that dynamic programming can compute its exact optimal values. We call that exact solution the oracle and use it as an answer key. Every learner and planner in this chapter is graded against it, so we always know how close a method got, not just whether its output looks reasonable.
This chapter bends one rule from the earlier chapters. There, learners were never allowed to look at the model. Here planners are allowed to use one - that is what planning means. But the model a planner gets is always one of two things: a model it learned from its own experience, or one we explicitly hand it. Either way, the grading still comes from the oracle.
